accepted.s: Under Article 243D(3) of the Constitution, the minimum reservation for women in seats of Panchayats is:
o: One-half of the total seats, excluding SC/ST seats
One-third of the total seats, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs
accepted.x: Article 243D(3) provides that not less than one-third of the total seats in every Panchayat, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs, shall be reserved for women.
accepted.tq: Test the constitutional minimum against the higher reservation adopted by some States.
accepted.sec: Reservation for women in PRIs - constitutional minimum, States providing 50%

accepted.s: Reservation of not less than one-third of the total number of offices of chairpersons in Panchayats for women is provided under:
accepted.x: Article 243D(4) provides reservation of not less than one-third of the offices of chairpersons in Panchayats for women.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between adjacent constitutional clauses dealing with seats and chairperson posts.
accepted.sec: Reservation for women in PRIs - constitutional minimum, States providing 50%

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding reservation in Panchayats is correct?
o: Rotation is permitted only for chairperson posts.
Reserved seats are allotted by rotation.
Reserved seats are permanently allotted to the same constituencies.
Only seats reserved for SCs and STs are rotated.
accepted.x: Seats reserved under Article 243D are allotted by rotation among different constituencies or Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Use the exact constitutional mechanism rather than the broader reservation percentage.
accepted.sec: Reservation for women in PRIs - constitutional minimum, States providing 50%

accepted.s: Which State was the first to provide 50 per cent reservation for women in local bodies?
accepted.x: Bihar was the first State mentioned as having raised reservation for women in local bodies to 50 per cent, in 2006.
accepted.tq: Test the first-adopter trap among States that subsequently provided 50 per cent reservation.
accepted.sec: Reservation for women in PRIs - constitutional minimum, States providing 50%

accepted.s:
Which of the following States or Union Territories was listed as meeting exactly the 50 per cent quota for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions?
1. Andhra Pradesh
2. Gujarat
3. Himachal Pradesh
4. Sikkim
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and Sikkim were listed as meeting the 50 per cent quota exactly. Gujarat was listed as short of 50 per cent, at 49.9 per cent.
accepted.tq: Separate the exact-50-per-cent group from the near-50-per-cent group.
accepted.sec: Reservation for women in PRIs - constitutional minimum, States providing 50%

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Sikkim was listed among the States meeting the 50 per cent quota exactly. The figure of 31.97 per cent was given for Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong numerical pairing by separating States from the Union Territory entry.
accepted.sec: Reservation for women in PRIs - constitutional minimum, States providing 50%

accepted.s: According to the cited Ministry of Panchayati Raj data, women constituted what proportion of the 24.41 lakh elected Panchayat representatives?
accepted.x: Of 24.41 lakh elected Panchayat representatives, 12.14 lakh were women, constituting 49.75 per cent.
accepted.tq: Calculate or recall the reported percentage rather than rounding it to the quota figure.
accepted.sec: Reservation for women in PRIs - constitutional minimum, States providing 50%

accepted.s: The Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan, mentioned in relation to 2026, is primarily intended to:
o: Fix OBC reservation through a dedicated commission
Conduct elections to Urban Local Bodies
Provide grants to State Finance Commissions
accepted.x: The Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan is intended to train women elected representatives.
accepted.tq: Identify the purpose of a named initiative from its target group and activity.
accepted.sec: Reservation for women in PRIs - constitutional minimum, States providing 50%

accepted.s: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 is primarily associated with:
accepted.x: The 73rd Amendment concerns rural Panchayati Raj Institutions, whereas the 74th Amendment concerns urban local bodies.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the closely related 73rd and 74th Amendments by rural and urban scope.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status to PRIs - amendment, commencement, National Panchayati Raj Day

accepted.s: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed on 24 April because on that date:
o: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment came into force
The 74th Constitutional Amendment came into force
The first State Finance Commission was constituted
accepted.x: 24 April marks the commencement of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, and is observed as National Panchayati Raj Day.
accepted.tq: Link an observance to the precise constitutional commencement event.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status to PRIs - amendment, commencement, National Panchayati Raj Day

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments?
o: The 73rd concerns urban bodies and the 74th concerns rural bodies.
The 73rd concerns rural bodies and came into force on 24 April 1993, while the 74th concerns urban bodies and came into force on 1 June 1993.
The 73rd concerns rural bodies and came into force on 1 June 1993, while the 74th concerns urban bodies and came into force on 24 April 1993.
Both amendments came into force on 24 April 1993.
accepted.x: The 73rd Amendment relates to rural Panchayats and commenced on 24 April 1993. The 74th relates to urban local bodies and commenced on 1 June 1993.
accepted.tq: Compare both amendments across subject and commencement date.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status to PRIs - amendment, commencement, National Panchayati Raj Day

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 1989 failed in the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Panchayati Raj bill introduced in 1991 by P. V. Narasimha Rao became the 73rd Amendment.
3. The 73rd Amendment gave constitutional shape to Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 1989 Bill failed in the Rajya Sabha, while the 1991 initiative under P. V. Narasimha Rao resulted in the 73rd Amendment and gave effect to Article 40.
accepted.tq: Test the legislative history through a sequence of linked constitutional developments.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status to PRIs - amendment, commencement, National Panchayati Raj Day

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The 73rd Constitutional Amendment is a landmark in the evolution of grassroots democracy in India.
Reason (R): It brought Panchayati Raj Institutions into the justiciable part of the Constitution and promoted participatory democracy.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: The assertion and reason are both true. Constitutional recognition and the shift from merely representative to participatory grassroots democracy explain the landmark character of the amendment.
accepted.tq: Check whether the constitutional consequence in the Reason explains the significance stated in the Assertion.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status to PRIs - amendment, commencement, National Panchayati Raj Day

accepted.s: A person is disqualified for being chosen as a member of a Panchayat if the person is disqualified under:
o: Only a law made by the Union Parliament
The law relating exclusively to Municipalities
Only the law relating to elections to Parliament
The law for elections to the State Legislature or a law made by the State Legislature
accepted.x: Article 243F refers to disqualification under the law for elections to the State Legislature or under a law made by the State Legislature.
accepted.tq: Ask which legislative framework supplies the disqualification rather than focusing only on age.
accepted.sec: Qualifications to contest (Article 243F)

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correct regarding a Panchayat constituted after an early dissolution?
o: It serves only for the remainder of the original term.
It always enjoys a fresh five-year term.
It continues until the next general election to the State Legislature.
It serves for six months only.
accepted.x: A Panchayat constituted after an early dissolution continues only for the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued.
accepted.tq: Reject the tempting but incorrect assumption that every newly elected Panchayat gets a fresh full term.
accepted.sec: Term, dissolution and fresh elections (Article 243E)

accepted.s: The State Finance Commission for Panchayats is constituted by the Governor:
accepted.x: Under Article 243I, the Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission every five years. The first Commission was to be constituted within one year of 24 April 1993.
accepted.tq: Use the recurring constitutional interval and distinguish it from the first-constitution deadline.
accepted.sec: State Finance Commission - Article 243I

accepted.s: The first State Finance Commission under Article 243I was required to be constituted within:
o: Two years of the first Panchayat election
Five years of the Constitution’s commencement
Six months of the commencement of the 73rd Amendment
accepted.x: The first State Finance Commission was required to be constituted within one year of 24 April 1993, the date on which the 73rd Amendment came into force.
accepted.tq: Separate the first-time limit from the normal five-year cycle.
accepted.sec: State Finance Commission - Article 243I

accepted.s: The State Finance Commission constituted under Article 243I also reviews the financial position of Municipalities under:
accepted.x: Article 243Y provides that the same State Finance Commission reviews the financial position of Municipalities as well.
accepted.tq: Match the rural finance provision with the corresponding urban finance provision.
accepted.sec: State Finance Commission - Article 243I

accepted.s:
Which of the following is NOT a function or recommendation associated with the State Finance Commission?
1. Distribution of net proceeds of State taxes, duties, tolls and fees between the State and local bodies
2. Grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of the State
3. Measures to improve the finances of Panchayats and Municipalities
4. Appointment of the State Election Commissioner
accepted.x: The State Finance Commission makes recommendations on fiscal distribution, assigned taxes, grants-in-aid and improvement of local finances. Appointment of the State Election Commissioner is not its function.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated constitutional authority among closely connected local-government functions.
accepted.sec: State Finance Commission - Article 243I

accepted.s: Who decides the composition and qualifications of members of a State Finance Commission?
o: The Governor by executive order alone
accepted.x: The State Legislature determines by law the composition of the State Finance Commission and the qualifications of its members.
accepted.tq: Apply the authority test: identify which institution has legislative power over composition and qualifications.
accepted.sec: State Finance Commission - Article 243I

accepted.s: Under Article 280(3)(bb) and (c), the Central Finance Commission may suggest measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State on the basis of:
o: Reports of the District Planning Committee
Reports of the State Election Commission
Reports of the State Finance Commission
Reports of the Union Public Service Commission
accepted.x: The Central Finance Commission may recommend measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities on the basis of State Finance Commission recommendations.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the financial roles of the State and Central Finance Commissions.
accepted.sec: State Finance Commission - Article 243I

accepted.s: Reservation of seats and offices of chairpersons for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Panchayats is made broadly in proportion to their:
o: Share in the State’s total population only
Population in the area of the Panchayat at every level
Share among elected Panchayat members in the previous election
accepted.x: Article 243D provides for reservation for SCs and STs in proportion to their population in the Panchayat area, at every level.
accepted.tq: Distinguish area-wise population proportion from State-wide political representation.
accepted.sec: Reservation of seats (Article 243D)

accepted.s: Which State is exempt from reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes in Panchayats because it has no Scheduled Caste population?
accepted.x: Arunachal Pradesh is exempt from SC reservation because it has no Scheduled Caste population.
accepted.tq: Test the specific constitutional exception rather than the general reservation rule.
accepted.sec: Reservation of seats (Article 243D)

accepted.s: In K. Krishna Murthy v. Union of India (2010), the Constitution Bench upheld the constitutional validity of provisions enabling reservation for backward classes in local bodies under:
accepted.x: K. Krishna Murthy upheld the provisions contained in Articles 243D(6) and 243T(6), while distinguishing political backwardness from social and educational backwardness.
accepted.tq: Match the case with the precise constitutional provisions involved.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in local bodies - K. Krishna Murthy and Vikas Kishanrao Gawali

accepted.s: The distinction emphasised in K. Krishna Murthy between political backwardness and social or educational backwardness is relevant to:
o: Reservation for backward classes in local bodies
The distribution of State taxes to Municipalities
The appointment of State Election Commissioners
accepted.x: The case clarified that political representation in local bodies involves a distinct constitutional consideration from social and educational backwardness.
accepted.tq: Apply the judicial distinction to the subject area in which it operates.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in local bodies - K. Krishna Murthy and Vikas Kishanrao Gawali

accepted.s:
The triple test laid down in Vikas Kishanrao Gawali v. State of Maharashtra (2021) includes which of the following?
1. A dedicated commission conducting rigorous empirical inquiry
2. Fixation of local-body-wise reservation based on the findings
3. Keeping the aggregate SC, ST and OBC reservation within 50 per cent
4. Automatic reservation of 50 per cent for OBCs in every local body
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 constitute the triple test. Statement 4 is false because the judgment does not provide for automatic 50 per cent OBC reservation in every local body.
accepted.tq: Use the three-part test and reject the absolute automatic-quota statement.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in local bodies - K. Krishna Murthy and Vikas Kishanrao Gawali

accepted.s: The total vertical reservation for SCs, STs and OBCs in local bodies, as stated in relation to the decisions in K. Krishna Murthy and Vikas Kishanrao Gawali, is normally subject to a ceiling of:
accepted.x: The decisions refer to the general ceiling that the aggregate vertical reservation for SCs, STs and OBCs should not ordinarily exceed 50 per cent.
accepted.tq: Recall the aggregate ceiling while avoiding confusion with the one-third women’s minimum.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in local bodies - K. Krishna Murthy and Vikas Kishanrao Gawali

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved what level of BC reservation in rural and urban local bodies, respectively?
o: 33⅓ per cent in rural and 34 per cent in urban local bodies
50 per cent in rural and 34 per cent in urban local bodies
34 per cent in rural and 33⅓ per cent in urban local bodies
34 per cent in both rural and urban local bodies
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved 34 per cent BC reservation in rural local bodies and 33⅓ per cent in urban local bodies.
accepted.tq: Compare the two percentages in their correct rural–urban order.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in local bodies - K. Krishna Murthy and Vikas Kishanrao Gawali

accepted.s: Which Government Order notified a 33.33 per cent BC quota for Urban Local Body elections in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 notified the 33.33 per cent BC quota for Urban Local Body polls in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact order number associated with the notified urban quota.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in local bodies - K. Krishna Murthy and Vikas Kishanrao Gawali

accepted.s: Part VI of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 gives effect to which constitutional provision?
accepted.x: Part VI of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 gives effect to Article 243I relating to the State Finance Commission.
accepted.tq: Match the State legislation with the specific constitutional article it implements.
accepted.sec: AP State Finance Commissions - number and reports
